insight: Foreground sleeps (Start-Sleep/sleep N before a check) are harness-blocked. Waiting on CI/deploys: run_in_background + blocking command (gh run watch --exit-status) for one notification, Monitor until-loop for polling, or direct sleep-free status query. summary: Hot-path fire-and-forget captures must be guarded+detached, not inline-awaited. @astragenie/gepa-core ships raw .ts; first dynamic import cold-parses the provider tree (multi-sec) — writeArtifact paid it ~10x/ceremony. Fix: fireGuarded(fn,ms) + trackDetached (runner-plugin#360).
detail: writeArtifact inline-awaited unguarded fireCaptureTeeSilent on every artifact write; cold @astragenie/gepa-core .ts parse blocked each. Fix merged 6fb35ece: shared fireGuarded timeout-race helper + writeArtifact detaches both fire-and-forget captures (trackDetached + terminal .catch). How-to-apply: never inline-await a best-effort dynamic-import path on a hot path; guard with timeout AND detach. Root cure: ship compiled dist not raw .ts.

summary: Promise.race bounds the LOGICAL await, NOT OS-process wall-time (loser isn't cancelled). Bun/Windows: an unref'd timer raced against a zero-handle promise never fires — the test hangs forever. Test wall-time via child-process timing; race tests against slow-but-real competitors.
detail: A pending import + ref'd setTimeout keep the event loop alive past the race's logical resolution. Bun-on-Windows: new Promise(()=>{}) holds zero handles so nothing pumps the loop to fire an unref'd timer -> a guarded-fire test ran 69min zombie. For a real wall-time bound: detach + .unref() timers; assert via child-process total wall time (~1.1s vs ~6s), never inert stand-ins.

summary: Claude Code PreToolUse hooks: hookSpecificOutput MUST include hookEventName:'PreToolUse' or the harness rejects the whole payload and the hook silently no-ops. dev-team#176: model-routing enforce omitted it -> FEAT-194 S2b injection dead -> builds silently fell back to Opus.
detail: Non-fatal (hook error swallowed) so easy to miss; the symptom is a cost regression, not a failure. How-to-apply: any hook emitting hookSpecificOutput must set hookEventName; add a unit assertion on the field.

summary: Crew builder subagents die mid-job at ~65-85 tool calls / ~18-22min, truncating mid-thought with no handoff and uncommitted (sometimes broken) WIP; orphaned hung child procs zombie ~69min then fire a stale completed-notification (dev-team#174/#179).
detail: Recovery that works: auto-resume the SAME agent via SendMessage with a git-state snapshot (status/log) — it keeps context and finishes cleanly. Expect to manually kill leftover bun/node + MCP procs at session close; the harness does not reap them (Claude Code CLI concern, not plugin-fixable).

summary: Cross-repo landing-gate: work fully visible in one repo can be unmergeable because its CI/publish gate lives in ANOTHER. FEAT-190 blocked (dev-team CI = astragenie/common reusable-plugin-ci.yml npm ci); FEAT-185 S-B blocked (gepa-core publish in plugins-common). Do cross-repo hal

summary: astramem project scoping: crew astramemProvider scopes to memory.project (loop.json, e.g. 'dev-team'); the astramem CLI has NO --project flag -> uses a default scope. CLI-stored and provider-stored memories are mutually invisible (astramem-plugin#33). Verify: astramemProvider wri
detail: astramemProvider.recall() reads the JSONL fallback when dualWrite:true (ranking fidelity) and reads astramem directly only when dualWrite:false — so a dualWrite:true recall does NOT prove the astramem write. To test the astramem leg, use dualWrite:false. Operator CLI remember/recall land in a different project than agents recall from; fix = --project flag on the CLI (astramem-plugin#33).
